grand_strategy.reading: The Holy See has no army and no military allies, so its grand strategy is diplomatic and moral: keep 184 states talking to it, keep the Church alive where it is restricted, and make the pope's voice count in wars it cannot stop. Under Leo XIV, elected on 8 May 2025 as the first American-born pope, the line continues Francis but is sharper on migration and Gaza, and it accepts cooler relations with Washington as the price. The weak points are money (a structural deficit covered by Peter's Pence) and China, where the 2018 deal is the main file and the clearest case of a channel kept open at the cost of its text. Recognition is the currency it trades: Taiwan (one of the few states with relations with the Republic of China), Palestine since 2015, and the Lebanon and Turkey trip of late 2025 as a way to speak to Middle East Christians. Non-events to watch: no US visit was planned for 2026, and the Ukraine talks offer in Vatican City has not been accepted by Moscow.

stances.note: Italy surrounds the enclave and the Lateran Treaty (ratified 7 Jun 1929) and the 1984 revised concordat set the terms. No alliance: the Holy See is not in a military arrangement with Rome, and the 1984 revision ended Catholicism as state religion. Bond - kin: a shared Roman and Catholic history. Grade is our reading of the treaty structure (confidence B, one tier-1 source for diplomatic relations).

stances.note: Full diplomatic relations and an embassy to the Holy See (Ambassador Brian Burch, per Wikipedia index). The grade is partner because the link is transactional on migration, peace and religious freedom, not alignment. Trend cooling since Leo XIV was elected on 8 May 2025: his backing of the US bishops against the migration crackdown (Nov 2025) and Vance calling the Vatican views troubling. Bond - affinity: a shared American Catholic constituency, not kinship with the state. The pope said in Feb 2026 he would not visit the US that year (single tier-4 pointer, not used as a source).

stances.note: No diplomatic relations with the People's Republic; the Holy See recognises the Republic of China (Taiwan). The provisional agreement on bishops (signed Sept 2018, renewed 2020, 2022 and on 22 Oct 2024 for four years to 2028) is cooperation the Holy See accepts out of necessity while Beijing has breached it by appointing bishops alone (Shanghai, the Jiangxi diocese). That is the reluctant grade. Bond - grievance: the underground Church and the 2018 deal mark an open wound. The renewal text is unpublished, so the reading rests on the Holy See statement as reported.

stances.note: Mediator and humanitarian channel, not alignment: Zelenskyy met Leo XIV at Castel Gandolfo on 9 Jul 2025, thanked the Vatican for returning children taken to Russia, and both proposed the Vatican as a venue for talks. Cardinal Zuppi is the papal envoy. Warming since the meeting; the Vatican does not take sides on the war in treaty terms. Bond - kin: the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church is in full communion with Rome, a shared faith (the kin reading is ours, confidence C).

stances.note: Diplomatic relations since 2009 (Wikipedia index, tier 4), largely tied to ecumenical relations with the Russian Orthodox Church. Neutral is our reading (confidence C): no source uses the word. Bond - none: pure interest in access and in the Ukrainian children file.

stances.note: Nicaragua expelled the nuncio in March 2022, the Vatican closed its Managua embassy in March 2023, and Nicaragua has suspended relations (Wikipedia index). Ortega has cancelled Church legal status and expelled bishops (Herrera, Nov 2024; received by Leo XIV in exile, Aug 2025). The Holy See aims at protecting the Church, not at the end of the regime. No source uses the word rival: the grade is our reading of the structure (confidence C). Bond - grievance: a persecution wound on the Church side.
